help.where.river.name: River
help.where.discard.name: Discard pile
help.where.territory.name: Territory
help.where.river: This card is revealed in the River. To develop it, drag it onto the card of your territory you want to replace (same position). End of game: when 2 piles are depleted, or when a player declares it while a pile is depleted.
help.where.discard: The replaced or discarded cards, face up (the last one on top).
help.where.territory: Your territory: 5 cards in your Line (face up) and 5 in your Hand (hidden from your opponent), positions 1 to 5. Adjacent: left, right, and the card directly in front or behind (same position, Line ↔ Hand).
help.hidden.pile.name: River draw pile
help.hidden.pile: The face-down cards of the pile: its thickness shows how many are left. When the revealed card is taken, the next one is revealed.
help.hidden.gift.name: Card received
help.hidden.gift: The Development card your opponent gives you at the start of the game: it goes into your Hand.
help.hidden.hidden.name: Hand card
help.hidden.hidden: A card in your opponent's Hand: you will not see it until the end of the game. Each player's Hand is hidden from their opponent.
help.1.rule: Count the Mountains in your territory at the end of the game.
help.2.rule: Each Naishi only scores if she is in the central column of your territory (position 3).
help.3.rule: Each Advisor scores points depending on his position, from left to right, whether in your Line or in your Hand.
help.3.bonus: He also scores 4 points per adjacent Naishi.
help.4.rule: Each Fort on the left or right extremity of your territory (position 1 or 5, in your Line or Hand) scores 6 points.
help.5.alone: A Sentinel not adjacent to another Sentinel scores 3 points.
help.5.bonus: She also scores 4 points per adjacent Fort.
help.7.rule: Each Monk scores 5 points if he is in your Hand.
help.7.bonus: He also scores 2 points per adjacent Torii.
help.8.rule: Count the groups of adjacent Rice fields.
help.8.groups: If you have 2 groups, each of them scores.
help.9.rule: Count the Banners in your Line: those in your Hand do not count.
help.10.rule: Each Horseman scores 3 points if he is in your Hand.
help.10.bonus: If you have a Banner in your Line in the same position, he scores 10 more points.
help.11.rule: Each Ronin scores according to the number of different cards with a rectangular or hexagonal frame in your territory.
help.11.except: Mountains and Ninjas do not count. With the expansion, the Ryokan counts as one more Province.
help.12.rule: At the end of the game, you choose a character in your territory: the Ninja copies its colour and scoring conditions.
help.12.limits: A Ninja cannot copy another Ninja or a Legend card. If you have no character to copy, it scores no points and has no icon.
help.13.rule: The Legendary Naishi scores 10 points in specific places: the centre of the Line, the centre of the Hand and both extremities of the Line.
help.14.rule: If you have no Naishi, the Legendary Advisor scores 5 points per Advisor in your territory (himself included). If you have a Naishi, he scores 0 points.
help.15.alone: A Legendary Sentinel not adjacent to another Sentinel scores 5 points.
help.15.bonus: She also scores 3 points per Fort and per Rice field in the same row (Line or Hand).
help.16.rule: The Legendary Horseman scores 4 points per adjacent Province, and 4 more points per adjacent Banner: an adjacent Banner is therefore worth 8 points to him.
help.17.rule: The Legendary Monk scores 2 points per adjacent character.
help.17.icons.title: Two icons
help.17.icons: This card has 2 icons: it counts both as a Monk and as a Torii.
help.18.rule: The Legendary Ronin scores according to the longest series of identical cards with a rectangular or hexagonal frame in your territory. Mountains do not count.
help.19.rule: At the end of the game, you choose a character of your opponent: the Legendary Ninja copies its colour and scoring conditions.
help.19.limits: It cannot copy a Ninja or a Legend card. If your opponent has no character, it scores no points.
help.traveller.enter: When you take this card from the River (not through a switch or a decree).
help.traveller.leave: When you discard it by replacing it with a development (not when it is switched).
help.traveller.reminder: A Traveller has no points and no icon. Its effect is optional.
help.20.effect: You may swap 2 cards anywhere in your territory.
help.21.effect: You may recall your Emissaries from the Imperial Court, except the one on the Imperial Decree, which stays locked.
help.22.effect: You may swap 2 cards anywhere in your territory.
help.23.effect: You may immediately develop one more card. The pile card that just replaced the Little Girl is only revealed at the end of the action: you can only choose from the other 4 piles.
help.24.effect: You may recall your Emissaries from the Imperial Court, except the one on the Imperial Decree.
help.25.effect: You take the Ryokan (even from your opponent) and place it on its 7-point side. This is automatic.
help.ryokan.name: Ryokan
help.ryokan.rule: When a Traveller card enters your territory from the River, you take the Ryokan on its 4-point side. If you already have it on its 4-point side, flip it to its 7-point side.
help.ryokan.end: At the end of the game
help.ryokan.score: It is worth 4 or 7 points, counts as one more Province for the Ronin, and its colour (black) counts for the tie-breaker. It is adjacent to no card.
help.ryokan.extension: The Ryokan is part of the <ext>Legends & Travellers</ext> expansion.
help.traveller.intro: This card is a Traveller from the Legends & Travellers expansion.
help.traveller.ryokan: Each time a Traveller enters your territory from the River, you take the <ryokan>Ryokan</ryokan> on its 4-point side, or flip it to its 7-point side if you already have it.
help.extension.name: Legends & Travellers
help.extension.intro: This game is played with the Legends & Travellers expansion: legendary characters with special scoring, and Travellers passing through who help you develop your territory.
help.extension.setup.legends: 3 Legends are drawn at random out of 7. Each one replaces a base copy of the same character: these 3 base cards are set aside here and are not played.
help.extension.setup.travellers: 5 Travellers are drawn at random out of 6; the last one is not played.
help.extension.setup.river: The Legends and Travellers are shuffled into the River only, after the Hands are dealt: each pile has 7 cards instead of 6. The end of the game does not change: it comes when 2 piles are depleted.
help.extension.legends.rule: A Legend is a character that scores differently from the base character. Click a card to see its scoring.
help.extension.legends.ninja: No Ninja, legendary or base, can copy a Legend.
help.extension.travellers.rule: Travellers have no points and no icon, and they are not characters (a Ninja cannot copy them). Each one has an effect, triggered at a specific moment. Click a card to see its effect.
help.extension.travellers.enter: On arrival (Cherry Blossom Lady, Porter, Samurai): when you take the Traveller from the River to develop your territory. Not when it arrives through a switch or an Imperial Decree.
help.extension.travellers.leave: On departure (Umbrella Lady, Old Man, Little Girl): when you discard it by replacing it with a card from the River. Not when it is switched.
help.extension.travellers.options: The effects are optional. If several effects trigger at the same time, you choose their order.
help.extension.ryokan: Each time a Traveller enters your territory from the River, you take the Ryokan on its 4-point side (even from your opponent). If you already have it on its 4-point side, you flip it to its 7-point side. At the end of the game, it counts as an 11th card in your territory.
help.court.name: Imperial Court
help.court.intro: On your turn: one main action, and one optional additional action with an Emissary. Drag an Emissary onto a circle to choose the action.
help.court.decree.name: Imperial Decree
help.court.decree: Exchange one of your cards with your opponent's card in the same position (Hand ↔ Hand, or Line ↔ Line). The Emissary is locked until the end of the game.
help.court.swap.name: Switch
help.court.swap: Switch 2 cards from the River, from your Line or from your Hand, or 1 card from your Hand with the card in the same position in your Line.
help.court.discard.name: Discard 2 River cards
help.court.discard: Discard 2 revealed cards from 2 different piles. The next cards are then revealed.
help.court.recall.name: Recall your Emissaries
help.court.recall: The button below the Court recalls all your Emissaries, except the one on the Imperial Decree. This is a main action. You may also declare the end of the game once a River pile is depleted.
help.playmat.name: Playmat
help.playmat.subscribers: Game Park subscribers can play with the playmat instead of the Imperial Court. Only the display changes, not the rules.
help.emissary.name: Emissary
help.emissary.rule: Each player has 2 Emissaries: black (flower) for the first player, white (tomoe) for the second. Sending an Emissary to the Imperial Court grants an action. It stays there until you recall your Emissaries.
help.emissary.cancel: As long as the action is not done, you can drag it back to your reserve.
help.first.name: First player
help.first.rule: The first player plays with the black Emissaries (flower) and starts the game. If the end of the game is triggered during their turn, the second player plays a final turn.
help.pad.name: Scorepad
help.pad.rule: At the end of the game, each player's points are written down line by line: flower column for the first player, tomoe column for the second.
help.pad.tie: In case of a tie, the player with the most different colours in their territory wins.
tutorial.ninja: A Ninja has appeared in the River! At the end of the game, it copies a character in your territory (Naishi, Advisor, Sentinel, Monk, Horseman or Ronin): it takes its colour and its points. If you have no character, it is worth nothing.
tutorial.pile: A River pile is depleted! The game ends when 2 piles are depleted. But as soon as one pile is depleted, you may also declare the end of the game instead of your main action, with the button at the top of the screen: your opponent then plays a final turn, and the points are counted.
tutorial.final: A red banner reminds you that the end of the game has been triggered. The final turn is played, then the points are counted.
tutorial.count: The Hands are revealed, the Ninjas copy a character, then the points are written on the scorepad, line by line. The player with the most points wins; in case of a tie, the one with the most different colours.
tutorial.copy: You have a Ninja: choose the character it copies with the “Copy” button of the card you want.
tutorial.1: Welcome to Naishi! You recruit characters and Provinces to develop your territory. Whoever scores the most points at the end of the game wins.
tutorial.2: This is your territory: a front Line of 5 cards, visible to all, and a back Hand of 5 cards, hidden from your opponent. For now, they are mostly Mountains. You can never freely reorganise your cards. At any time, click an element to learn more about it.
tutorial.3: This is the River. The top card of each pile can enter your territory, but only by replacing a card of your Line or Hand in the same position.
tutorial.4: To start, each player gives a Development card to their opponent. Choose the one you give; your opponent will do the same.
tutorial.5: Your Hand is shuffled at the start of the game.
tutorial.6: Your turn! To develop your territory, you must take a card from the River in the same position as the card of your Line or Hand you want to get rid of. Drag the Sentinel onto the card in position 2 of your Line or Hand.
tutorial.7: Developing is the main action of your turn. End your turn with the button at the top of the screen.
tutorial.8: Your opponent has played their turn and developed a card.
tutorial.9: Look at the Fort, in the middle of the River. At the end of the game, each Fort on an extremity of your territory (left or right) scores 6 points.
tutorial.10: But the Fort is in the central pile: if you take it now, it will go to the centre of your territory, where it scores nothing. Take it anyway in the centre of your Line; we will see how to move it.
tutorial.11: To move it, send an Emissary to a Switch space of the Imperial Court. Important: this optional action can be carried out before or after your development action.
tutorial.12: Switch exchanges 2 cards in the River, 2 cards in your Line, 2 cards in your Hand, or 2 cards of your Line and Hand in the same position. Drag the Fort onto the Mountain on the left extremity of your Line.
tutorial.13: Emissaries allow another additional action: Discard 2 River cards, from 2 different piles. But you are limited to one Emissary per turn.
tutorial.14: You have carried out your development action and an optional Emissary action: your turn ends by itself.
tutorial.15: By taking the Fort, you also revealed the next card: a Naishi! This card scores points in the central position.
tutorial.17: Your opponent took the Naishi and placed her in the centre of their Line: she is worth 12 points to them there.
tutorial.18: You would love to have this Naishi! The Imperial Decree is a unique action in the game. It lets you exchange one of your cards with your opponent's card in the same position, at the cost of your Emissary. Drag an Emissary onto the central space of the Imperial Court.
tutorial.19:
You can only exchange mirror cards (the central card of your Line for the central card of your opponent's Line).

Drag your central Mountain onto their Naishi. You take their Naishi, they take your Mountain.
tutorial.20: The Decree is a main action: your turn ends. The Decree Emissary stays locked on the Court until the end of the game.
tutorial.21: Your opponent plays their turn and develops a card.
tutorial.22: Use Recall my Emissaries to recall your Emissaries, but it will take your whole turn. The Decree Emissary will not come back.
tutorial.23: You know the essentials. Now play freely: develop your territory as you wish. The tutorial will resume when a River pile is depleted.
help.where.setAside.name: Cards not played
help.where.setAside: With the expansion, each Legend replaces the base card of the same character. These 3 base cards are not played: they are set aside, above the Ryokan. The ? button explains the rules of the expansion.
